condition: benign prostatic enlargement slow urinary stream hesitancy and waking 4 times nightly
level_rationale: Four months of a weak urinary stream accompanied by urinary hesitancy and waking 4 times nightly to urinate in a 67-year-old man indicates chronic lower urinary tract outflow symptoms warranting non-emergent outpatient general-physician evaluation rather than home self-care or emergency department treatment, whereas developing a painful full bladder while passing only drops of urine for 14 hours on top of 4 months of obstructive voiding symptoms indicates acute painful urinary retention requiring immediate ER bladder decompression.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact acute painful urinary retention escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4).

design_note: Four atomic reference facts state age 67 and male sex, 4 months of weak urinary stream, difficulty initiating urination, and waking 4 times nightly to urinate without naming prostatic hyperplasia, with a 1-word span difference (17 vs 18 words) and clean 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing. Under reviewer_notes Rule A and Rule D, replacing f4 ('wake 4 times a night to pee') with positive wording for acute painful urinary retention ('have a painful full bladder passing only drops for 14 hours') stays inside the same obstructive voiding case and escalates care unambiguously from outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) to ER catheterization (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
